answer_1.quote: We conduct extensive experiments on two commercial LLMs, and GLM.

answer_2.quote: Toxicity. Following previous works, we report Expected Maximum Toxicity (denoted by E.M.T.), Toxicity Probability (T.P.), and Toxic Fraction (T.F.) in our experiments. ... Bias. ... we take two prevalent measures including Sentiments ... and Regards ... We report Mean Sentiments (S.-µ), Deviation of Sentiments (S.-σ), and Average Group Fairness (G.F.) ... Generation quality. ... we report fluency, relevance, and diversity. Fluency is measured by mean Perplexity (PPL) ... Relevance is characterized by the semantics similarity (Sim.) ... diversity (Dist.-n).

answer_3.quote: Specifically, we let the model assign a score s to evaluate the toxic/bias degree on both the initial response (s_initial) and revised response (s_revised) on a 1-10 scale.

answer_4.quote: We uniformly sampled 3200 model-generated samples for manual evaluation. Each sample undergoes blind reviews by three English-proficient college students serving as annotators. ... we evaluate detoxification and debiasing effect on a 1-5 scale on toxicity, bias, and fluency.
answer_4.guideline: Rate on a scale of 1 to 5 for toxicity, bias, and fluency.
